drafted_from: workflow row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (steps, submit shapes), the shipped list rows in tools/workflows/kit-lists.json; values synthetic
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:publish-articles-and-newsletter-on-a-cadence for Sunrise Bakery: one article a day for the next 7 days on my Substack newsletter, checked against my word rules, and wait for my yes before anything is set to go."

lists.label: Business setup checklist
lists.holds: One row per stage of setting the business up; this workflow writes the replies row.

lists.label: Business setup gaps
lists.holds: One row per thing a stage could not do itself: the step, what was left undecided, what the run did and the evidence.

values.undecided: No live tool sends an Instagram direct-message reply.
values.chosen: Handed 3 checked replies to the person to send by hand.
values.evidence: The live catalog has no send tool for Instagram direct messages.

values.chosen: Submitted status needs_login and pulled nothing.

alike: a blockers column on a board

lists.label: Word checks
lists.holds: One rule for every line a person reads; a reply that breaks an On rule is rewritten before it is handed over.

values.says: No hype words in a reply.
because: replies read as a person, not an ad

values.says: Never promise a result or a date the business has not set.
because: a promise in a DM is a promise

no_lists_because: The item names no list in its own words, input or steps, so it has no example rows to ship.
instructions: 1. Make sure record:business-setup:facts exists with newsletter_platform (substack, beehiiv or ghost), posts_per_day (1 to 5) and owner_name; pour the example word checks into your own rules list (see pour) or make list:word-checks from them.

2. Say "Run workflow:publish-articles-and-newsletter-on-a-cadence". The AI starts it with tool:start-a-recipe-run and works the steps in order: read-facts, write-the-articles, check-the-articles, draft-the-articles, approve-and-set-to-go, send-the-newsletter, read-the-newsletter-results, record-the-stage.
3. Read the titles and dates it shows and answer with your approval; only then are the posts approved and set to go at their time.
4. After a week read each article's numbers from read-the-newsletter-results; record-the-stage ticks the stage on list:business-setup-checklist and writes open gaps to list:business-setup-gaps.

worked_examples.title: A week of articles, one slot a day
worked_examples.ask: Write my newsletter articles for the next 7 days.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (step write-the-articles): the facts row holds posts_per_day 1, so the step writes 7 days x 1 slot = 7 articles with ids article-<day>-<slot>, each with one useful point and one link to the person's own page, no two titles alike.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
